meta.name: Rimrock Mesa
meta.note: Generated by tools/genworld.mjs; safe to hand-edit.

hello.text: Mesa. I keep rain by the jar because the sky seldom keeps appointments. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: Three jars full. That counts as a wet season here.

hello.text: Flint. I polish stone until it admits the sky was there first. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: That shine is honest work, not water.

hello.text: Sora. I make bitter oil from the juniper that survives the rim. That's my place behind me. Come say hello before you let yourself in.

again.text: A drop is medicine. Two drops are a lesson.

text: Careful. It is a long way down and it does not look it from here.
Bly. I sit at the edge and count weather coming. Somebody has to, and nobody else will.

third.text: Back at the edge. It grows on you or it does not.

text: Red dirt, and more red dirt, and the shadow of this rock crossing it twice a day.
Nothing lives down there that would not rather be up here.

off.text: Not one you would walk. That is rather the point of the place.

trade.text: I build cairns with them. Four is a good cairn. Here.

after.text: Weather still coming. It always is.

text: You came up the cut. Good. Most look at it and decide they have seen enough.
Wend. I garden on a rock in a drought, which everyone here thinks is funny.

welcome.text: Up on the cap again. The wind is honest up here.

choices.text: Where does the water come from?

gift.text: Take them. They come up in the cracks where the rock holds the night cold.

text: The seep, south of the yard. One seep, and everything on this table drinks from it.
The wash below it runs twice a year and we all go and watch.
Sand gets in everything up here. Everything. I make a living out of that.
Pike. Door's open now I know your face -- it sticks, put your shoulder in it.
There is a porch inside the door. Stamp in there and not on my floor, and we will get on.

welcome.text: Come in out of the grit whenever you like. Shut the inner door behind you.

sifteragain.text: You have been at my sifter. I can hear it from the road when it is still turning.

choices.text: Why a porch inside the house?

breaks.text: Hinges. Then axles. Then people, but they mend slower and pay worse.

trade.text: Juniper? I will take that. It splits clean and it does not warp.

text: Sifter. Everything that comes off this mesa comes to me full of grit and leaves without it.
Turn it if you like. It gives back pebbles, mostly, and once in a while somebody else's money.
Because a door on a mesa is a hole, and a hole lets in a mesa.
Two doors and a room between them. It is the single best thing in that house and it is empty on purpose.

hello.text: Agate. Stone Stacker up here on the rim. The view's free; the shade costs you a conversation.

again.text: A good wall wants no mortar and no hurry.

hello.text: You climbed the whole way -- good. Bluff, Dust Sweeper. Mine's the house holding that wall up.

again.text: It's not the heat, it's the geology.

hello.text: Chert. I keep at it as Cairn Keeper. The mesa was here first and it doesn't let you forget.

again.text: Every stone in that wall has a name. I was bored.

hello.text: Mind the scree past my fence. Cobble -- Echo Counter. Water's in the shade barrel if you need it.

again.text: The rim glows red at sundown. Never gets old.

hello.text: Crag, Ridge Walker. Everything up here is either rock or on its way to being rock.

again.text: Found a fossil shaped like a smile. Kept it.

hello.text: Well met. Dusty. Been Fossil Sifter since the last rockfall rearranged the road.

again.text: The wind up here has opinions.
